cards.design_implication: If the research objective requires 3D atomic positioning with ~19 pm precision and the sample is compatible with AET, then AET combined with atom-tracing algorithms may be considered as a candidate method.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Furthermore, the combination of AET and atom-tracing algorithms has enabled the determination of the coordinates of individual atoms and point defects in materials with a 3D precision of ~19 pm, allowing direct measurements of 3D atomic displacements and the full strain tensor.
limitations: The excerpt reports the existence of this capability but does not define specific sample eligibility criteria, instrument settings, or the experimental conditions required to achieve this precision.
cards.statement: Atomic electron tomography (AET) combined with atom-tracing algorithms has enabled the determination of atomic coordinates and point defects in materials with a 3D precision of approximately 19 picometers.

cards.design_implication: When designing a study for physical science samples where single-particle averaging is proposed, one must verify that the sample consists of identical copies and address challenges related to diffraction and phase contrast in TEM images.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Although single-particle cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has been under rapid development for 3D structure determination of macromolecules with identical or similar conformations at near-atomic resolution, this method cannot be generally applied to the physical sciences for the following three reasons. First, most materials do not have identical copies and cannot be averaged to achieve atomic resolution. Second, a priori knowledge of the peptide sequence and stereochemistry in protein molecules greatly facilitates their 3D atomic structure determination, but this knowledge is not applicable to physical science samples. Third, unlike in biological specimens, the presence of diffraction and phase contrast in the transmission electron microscopy images of most materials poses a challenge for tomographic reconstruction.
limitations: The statement describes general challenges and reasons for limited applicability, not definitive impossibility for all physical science samples.
cards.statement: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy is generally not applicable to physical science samples because materials lack identical copies for averaging, lack a priori knowledge of peptide sequences/stereochemistry, and exhibit diffraction and phase contrast that challenge tomographic reconstruction.
